items.q: What is Inspire BD IT?
items.a: Inspire BD IT is an ERP software company in Bangladesh and a member of BASIS. We build cloud-based ERP software that brings accounting, inventory, sales, purchase, production, HR and payroll into one system, and we have delivered 450+ ERP projects in Bangladesh and abroad.

items.q: Does Inspire BD IT have AI features?
items.a: Yes. ERP AI is live in Inspire BD IT: an AI assistant you can ask in plain English, AI agents that do routine work, AI-written reports, document AI for bills and invoices, demand and sales forecasting, anomaly and fraud detection, smart reorder, and HR and cash-flow AI. Explore ERP AI →

items.q: What can I ask the ERP AI assistant?
items.a: Questions about your own ERP data, in English: for example "who are our top 10 customers by due this month?" or "show stock value by warehouse as a chart". It answers with numbers, tables or charts. About the AI Assistant →

items.q: Do ERP AI agents act without approval?
items.a: No. Agents prepare the work, such as draft purchase orders, payment reminders and approval requests, and your team reviews and approves important actions in the ERP. About AI Agents →

items.q: Which modules does the ERP include?
items.a: Accounts, inventory and warehouse, sales, purchase and e-procurement, production, HRM and payroll, CRM and customer portal, POS, billing, fixed assets, import and export LC, KPI and MIS dashboards, and more. You start with the modules you need and add others later.

items.q: Which industries do you work with?
items.a: Garments and textiles, accessories, pharmaceutical, FMCG, food and beverage, manufacturing, mills and factories, trading and distribution, retail and wholesale, real estate, agro, jute, electrical, power and energy, hotels, universities, government and SMEs.

items.q: Is Inspire BD IT cloud-based?
items.a: Yes. Inspire BD IT is a cloud (SaaS) ERP, so your team works in a web browser from the office, the factory or home, and there is no software to install on each computer.

items.q: Is it suitable for small businesses?
items.a: Yes. Small and medium businesses can start with core modules such as accounts, inventory and sales, and grow into HR, payroll or production when they need them.

items.q: Can the ERP be adapted to how my company works?
items.a: Yes. During implementation we set up your company structure, approval steps, reports and user roles. Specific features for your business can be discussed in the demo.

items.q: How long does implementation take?
items.a: It depends on the number of modules, users and branches, and on how much data you bring over. After a requirement meeting we agree a plan and a go-live date with you.

items.q: Do you provide training and support?
items.a: Yes. Our implementation team trains every user group on the modules they use, and our support team stays with you after go-live.

items.q: How is our data kept secure?
items.a: Each user only sees what their role allows: permissions are set per user and per module in the user management module, and changes are recorded for audit.

items.a: Fill in the demo request form, or call +880 1617-224424, and we will arrange a live demo with the modules that matter to your business.

posts.title: Cloud ERP vs On-Premise: 2026 Cost-Benefit Analysis
posts.excerpt: Comparative analysis showing how cloud ERP reduces IT costs by 40% while improving scalability - complete with ROI calculator for your business size.
posts.content:
## 1. Total Cost of Ownership Comparison

The 2026 cost landscape shows significant differences between deployment models:

Average 5-Year Savings: 40% with Cloud ERP Cost Factor Cloud ERP On-Premise ERP Initial Implementation Lower (No hardware costs) High (Servers, infrastructure) IT Staff Requirements Reduced by 60-70% Dedicated team needed Software Updates Automatic, included Manual, additional costs Scalability Instant, pay-as-you-grow Costly hardware upgrades Disaster Recovery Built-in redundancy Additional infrastructure 5-Year TCO (Mid-size business) $250,000 $420,000 2026 Insight: The break-even point for cloud ERP has moved to just 14 months for most businesses, down from 22 months in 2022.

## 2. ROI Analysis by Business Size

Cloud ERP delivers different value propositions based on organization size:

### Quick ROI Estimator

Use this simple formula to estimate your potential savings: Annual Savings = (Current IT Budget × 0.4) + (Productivity Gains × Employee Count × $8,500) Where 0.4 represents the 40% average IT cost reduction and $8,500 is the average productivity gain per employee.

### Small Businesses (1-50 employees)

Key benefit: Enterprise features without enterprise costs Modern cloud ERP interface designed for small businesses

- Average implementation time: 2-4 weeks
- Typical 3-year ROI: 220-280%

### Mid-Market (50-500 employees)

- Average implementation time: 6-10 weeks
- Typical 3-year ROI: 180-220%
- Key benefit: Scalability during growth periods

posts.title: ERP AI: how an AI assistant and AI agents work inside your ERP
posts.excerpt: ERP AI is live in Inspire BD IT. How the AI assistant answers in plain English, how agents do routine work, and where to start.
posts.content:
## Why AI belongs inside the ERP

Your ERP already holds the most reliable picture of your business: every sale, purchase, stock movement, payment and payroll run. An AI tool that sits outside the ERP has to be fed exports and copies. ERP AI works where the data already is, with the same users and roles as your ERP, so it can answer from live numbers and hand work to the right person.

## 1. The AI Assistant: ask instead of searching

Most ERP questions are simple to ask and slow to answer: find the right report, set the filters, export, sort. With the AI Assistant you ask in plain English and get a number, a table or a chart.

“Who are our top 10 customers by outstanding due this month?”

- “Which products sold less this quarter than last quarter?”
- “Show stock value by warehouse as a chart.”

Follow-up questions keep the context, so “now only the Dhaka branch” works the way you would expect.

## 2. AI Agents: from answers to actions

An answer is useful; work done is better.

AI Agents

watch the ERP for moments that need action and prepare the work: a draft purchase order when stock reaches its reorder level, a reminder to a customer whose invoice is overdue, a nudge to a manager whose approval is waiting.

People stay in control. Agents prepare and route; your team reviews and approves important actions in the ERP. The result is less typing, chasing and remembering, and fewer things that slip through the cracks.

## 3. Predictions and early warnings

Because ERP AI learns from your own history, it can look ahead:

Demand & sales forecasting

predicts sales by product, branch, area and season.

Smart reorder

suggests what to order and warns before stock-outs or expiry.

Cash-flow AI

predicts cash in and out for the coming weeks.

Anomaly & fraud detection

flags duplicate bills, unusual prices and stock mismatches.

## 4. Less typing with Document AI

Document AI

reads supplier invoices, bills, receipts and delivery challans and prepares the ERP entry for your team to check and post. The original document stays attached for audit.

## 5. Briefings instead of report piles

AI Reports & Insights

turns the numbers into a short daily or weekly briefing: what went up, what went down and what needs attention, with links to the reports behind it.

## Where to start

The quickest wins usually come from one department at a time:

Finance: Document AI for bills, anomaly detection for duplicate payments, and the cash-flow forecast.

Sales: the AI Assistant for daily questions and sales forecasting for planning.

Inventory and purchase: smart reorder with an agent that drafts the purchase orders.

HR: CV screening and attendance insights.

ERP AI works in English. See the full list of capabilities on the ERP AI page .

## See ERP AI on your own kind of data
